input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds only the Customer and is walk-away territory under the rule: it is an express no-hire ("hire, or employ"), it covers every Vendor employee rather than only personnel involved in the Services, it runs 24 months, and the phrase "regardless of how the employee applies" deliberately eliminates any general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It therefore fails the fallback (mutual, involvement-limited, 12 months, carve-outs, no no-hire) on every material term. It also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire anyone responding to general recruitment. Redline deletes the clause to reach the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), with the mutual 12-month fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Delete the one-sided 24-month no-hire imposed on Customer (§ 12.4)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 12.4: our position is that we do not accept a non-solicit or no-hire on the Customer, and this clause is a flat 24-month no-hire over every Vendor employee with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment and remain free to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. If Vendor needs protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no hiring restriction.
